title: Apostles' Gratitude
english: …They left behind what they had, which was their means of life, and they did not say to themselves, 'This is mere nonsense to us, and he discourses on excessive myths, promising to make us fishers of men' (Matthew 4:19).
But they let go even of these things, considering their nets and wealth as nothing, for their life was in their fishing nets and their hopes were sustained by the catch of fish.
Everything was theirs in their nets and all their wealth was in them, for they had their life in their nets; the catch of fish sustained their hopes for life.

And where such a thing is? Where can such a net be capable of hunting beasts? What lake or what sea brings men to us through nets? And what will be the profit of the hunt? Where will we use the catch after the hunt? But, paying attention to the one calling and having been made firm by faith and…
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment, beginning mid-sentence and ending mid-sentence; these are rendered with ellipses.
The clause 'λήρους ἡμῖν οὗτος καὶ μύθους περιττοὺς διαλέγεται, ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων καταστῆσαι ἐπαγγέλλεται' is a direct allusion to the rejection of Christ's call in the Gospels.
The sequence beginning 'Καὶ ποῦ τοιοῦτον δίκτυον...' consists of rhetorical questions regarding the nature of the miraculous catch and the subsequent utility of the harvest.
